scenes.say: So how do you build a track in Monaco, where people need these streets every single day?
You start six weeks before the race and do almost everything at night, so the city can drive by day.
In total that's more than twenty-one kilometres of barriers and twenty thousand square metres of fencing.
But the city never closes: around seven in the evening the streets reopen to normal traffic.
At six in the morning the roads close again and the race cars come out.
The track is narrow and there's almost nowhere to overtake, so qualifying decides everything.
The result: three point three kilometres, nineteen corners, and a race here since nineteen twenty-nine.

title: How to build an F1 track in Monaco
caption: Six weeks of night work, 21 km of barriers and streets that reopen every evening. Every track in 3D: lapradar.com
